title: SIGIL: Compiling Agent Skills into Typed Harnesses
exact_task: Compile prose SKILL.md procedures into typed executable agent harnesses and test mandated procedure execution versus prose consumption.
model_scale: gpt-4o and gpt-5; nine runs per skill per arm per model
runtime: AG-IR; deterministic lowering to Jac/OSP harness; code-owned gates plus model-owned typed operations
baselines: Prose SKILL.md in ReAct loop vs compiled harness; same authoring model/interface
data: 30 skills; three scenario tasks per skill; three repeats
evaluation: Applicable-Mandate Compliance; full-procedure completion; tokens; capability-axis comparison
distinction_from_flagship: Occupies typed compiler/runtime boundary, model/code ownership, source provenance and prose-vs-compiled causal enforcement; no fixed small renderer consuming authoritative supported/refuted/unknown/conflicting results or no-conclusion/copying controls.

title: SkillSmith: Compiling Agent Skills into Boundary-Guided Runtime Interfaces
exact_task: Compile heterogeneous skill packages offline into minimal executable boundary contracts and measure runtime cost/correctness across tasks, models and harnesses.
model_scale: Main GPT-5.5; cross-model GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, DeepSeek V4 Flash, Qwen3.6 35B A3B
runtime: Boundary-first compiler; typed operators/policies/validation/fallback; shared runtime
baselines: Raw-Skills; SkVM; no-skills context; paired same runtime/provider/tool environment
data: SkillsBench: 87 runnable tasks, 227 skill packages; seven verified representative tasks; five runs/condition
evaluation: Deterministic verifier success; tokens; calls; latency; cost proxy; path consistency; failure localization
distinction_from_flagship: Occupies offline compiler-runtime reuse by smaller/efficient models and executable boundary contracts; no four-state strict epistemic result contract or matched no-conclusion/copying decomposition.
evidence: arXiv:2605.15215v1 PDF §§4.1-4.4,B.3; primary PDF text lines 368-447,468-491,799-860; screenshot endpoint attempted and returned Cache miss

title: Ontology-to-tools Compilation for Executable Semantic Constraint Enforcement in LLM Agents
exact_task: Compile ontology specifications into executable MCP-aware tools used to extract, validate, repair and instantiate ontology-consistent knowledge graphs.
model_scale: Primary abstract does not state a fixed model scale; LLM agents in TWA proof-of-principle
runtime: Ontology-aware executable tools; MCP; persistent KG state; structured constraint feedback
baselines: Proof-of-principle case study; no matched raw/teacher/compiled fixed-student contrast stated
data: Metal-organic polyhedra synthesis literature; 30-paper case reported by the primary technical report
distinction_from_flagship: Occupies formal semantics compiled into executable LLM tools; targets constrained KG construction, not authoritative four-state query results rendered by a frozen small model.
evidence: arXiv:2602.03439v1 abstract; Cambridge Technical Report 343 primary page/report retrieved 2026-08-07

title: SkCC: Portable and Secure Skill Compilation for Cross-Framework LLM Agents
exact_task: Compile skills through a strongly typed intermediate representation into framework-specific executable artifacts while checking portability/security constraints.
model_scale: Primary abstract evaluates Claude Code and Kimi CLI; exact underlying model scales are not stated in the abstract
runtime: SkIR compiler and compile-time analyzer targeting heterogeneous agent frameworks
baselines: Native/raw skill execution versus compiled cross-framework execution in SkillsBench-style evaluation
data: SkillsBench tasks across Claude Code and Kimi CLI reported by the paper
evaluation: Task pass rate, token/runtime efficiency, portability and security-analysis outcomes
distinction_from_flagship: Occupies typed skill IR and compile-time enforcement but not authoritative formal truth-status transport or independent strict-epistemic oracle.

title: SkillRT: Compiling Skills for Efficient Execution Everywhere
exact_task: Compile reusable skills by capability and optionally solidify runtime behavior into code for efficient execution across models and harnesses.
model_scale: Eight LLMs and three harnesses; exact model list retained in the primary paper
runtime: Skill compiler/runtime with capability compilation and JIT code solidification
baselines: Raw/interpreted skill execution versus compiled runtime variants
evaluation: Completion, tokens, latency, portability; JIT speed/latency outcomes
distinction_from_flagship: Occupies portable skill compilation and cross-model runtime efficiency; no four-state epistemic status or authoritative result-frame causal study.

title: Auto: The AGI Compiler

baselines: Original agent execution versus compiled/delegated execution
data: AUTO-BENCH: 560 spans plus a 300-item shifted stream reported
distinction_from_flagship: Occupies verified compilation of reusable agent behavior; not source-assertion-to-four-state result compilation or fixed-renderer interface placement.
